correctness.rationale: For all n>=2, the three exhaustive layer-parity configurations are proved necessary and sufficient for a dominating subset with induced perfect matching. Failure types are disjoint, and their exact binomial counts produce the polynomial. Every exceptional even-clique case is included. An independent vertex-level checker exhaustively corroborates every coefficient for n=2,...,7. Infinite validity comes from the structural proof.

evidence: The 2023 prism-stability paper studies changes to paired/total domination under vertex deletions, especially cycle prisms/hypercubes; such inequalities do not count the paired-dominating sets of all cardinalities in K_n square K_2.
The 2020 Cartesian complete-graph paper establishes total k-domination bounds and formulas, which impose a different condition and omit induced perfect matching.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Broader graph-product and prism theorems were assessed for dominating implication, not merely title overlap. Bounds and stability of minimum parameters do not imply the coefficient formula or the disjoint odd-layer obstruction; no stronger matching-enumeration theorem was found in the materially examined parts.
searches: paired domination of Cartesian product graphs complete graph K2 prism 2018 2023

evidence: This theorem supplies complete p_{n,k} for all n>=2, all k, including the exact failure obstruction and a universal cardinality threshold.

The cited 2013 work supplies general paired-domination inequalities, 2020 work different k-total domination, 2023 work stability; the 2016 abstract establishes polynomial vocabulary but does not specify complete prisms.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The new claim implies a scalar paired-domination minimum and all coefficient values, strictly more information than scalar bounds. The old results would imply the new claim only if they contained an all-set structural matching classification or equivalent coefficient theorem, which was not present in the checked scientific material. Abstract-only sources are named as residual risks.

evidence: Two-clique-with-perfect-matching is the Cartesian product K_n square K_2, as in the graph definition. The 2013 Cartesian-product paper treats inequalities for paired domination parameters, not all-size vertex-subset counts.
The coefficient derivation tracks odd-odd disjoint matching indices, which is lost when only the minimum cardinality is considered.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Checked both labels complete prism/Cartesian product and the equivalent occupation-by-layers description. A scalar paired-domination number or an ordinary domination polynomial cannot entail the all-size paired-domination polynomial without a further matching-structure theorem. No equivalent exact coefficient identity was identified in the material checked.

evidence: No indexed exact polynomial/table of complete prisms was found in these searches.
Direct independent enumeration for n=2,...,7 gives coefficients n=2:(4,1), n=3:(3,15,1), n=4:(4,62,28,1), n=5:(5,160,210,45,1); finite tables alone cannot prove novelty.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: Existing finite tables and small-case checks cannot cover a formula for all n. Failed searches are treated only as limited evidence, not a proof of uniqueness or priority.

originality.rationale: A complete coefficient formula and sharp large-even-set threshold were proved and compared by implication with relevant published Cartesian-product and prism domination results, paired-domination polynomial framework, semantic research records, and all accessible own-claim records. None of the materially examined theorems entails the full all-size enumeration. Global publication priority is uncertain due to named sources without inspectable full text.
residual_risks: No exhaustive global priority search or independent expert check.
Full text of the 2016 paired-domination polynomial conference work was not obtained; its specific standard families remain unknown.
Full text of the 2018 Goddard–Henning prism paper was not reliably accessed; the abstract alone cannot exclude complete-prism special cases.
Search indexing and accessible-page scope may omit relevant equivalent formulations or later literature.

value.rationale: The all-cardinality polynomial and exact failure classification solve a natural matching-constrained domination enumerator on an infinite Cartesian-product graph family. The sharp universal threshold for all sufficiently large even vertex subsets, the exceptional full-clique correction, and exact minimum multiplicities illuminate nontrivial structure beyond scalar domination bounds.
